title: Cross-validate: roundtrip parity
description: Cross-platform roundtrip validation. DONE - shared vectors
notes: 2026-08-25 roundtrip parity blocker: Python focused frame/vector/schema suite passes (240 passed, 10 skipped); Rust spec frame parse+roundtrip tests pass (2) and shared vector consumer passes (8), including every signed address mode and signed max payload. Read-only ctypes exercise of existing C lichen_frame_parse/write over current test/vectors/link_frame.json and link_frame_signed_modes.json: all 9 unsigned positives roundtrip exact; signed_encrypted rejects -EPROTONOSUPPORT and unsigned 256-byte over-max rejects -EMSGSIZE; but every modern signed positive (broadcast, short, extended, elided, and all max-payload variants: 9 total) rejects -EINVAL, so no signed parity. Root cause: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/frame.c:19/76-85 treats LLSec bit 7 as reserved and parses no 8-byte signer identifier; write path frame.c:139-142/183-190 forbids signer and keeps bit 7 clear. The current profile requires S and SI together and carries signer EUI-64. Existing clean C test passes only because lichen/tests/frame/main.c:334-383 hardcodes stale 0x20/0x21 signed frames without signer while labeling them current link_frame.json; current vectors use 0xA0/0xA1 and are 8 bytes longer. C production/header are current-phase read-only, so cannot close until C frame struct/parser/writer adopt SI/signing layout and the C test consumes current fixed corpus including signed max and negative categories.
